learn.title: Printing text
learn.body: `printf` prints exactly the characters inside its quotes. It does not add a new line by itself. If you want the next output to start on a new line, you must ask for one.

learn.title: Joining output
learn.body: Output continues where the last printf stopped.

learn.title: What that prints
learn.body: The first printf prints `one` and a new line. The second prints `two` with no new line, so the third continues on the same line. The output is two lines: `one` and then `two three`.

learn.title: Escape sequences
learn.body: A backslash inside a string starts an escape sequence, a special character. `\n` is a new line. `\t` is a tab. `\"` prints a double quote. `\\` prints one backslash.

learn.title: Escapes in use
learn.body: A quote needs a backslash, or it would end the string early.

learn.title: Reading an escape
steps: The text starts after the first quote
`\"` prints a literal double quote and does not end the string
The output is say "hi" followed by a new line
